---
title: "Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)"
description: "A neural-network architecture that processes sequences using a hidden state updated over time steps."
term: "Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)"
letter: "R"
category: "Deep Learning"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

A recurrent neural network processes a sequence one element at a time and
carries a state forward. That state gives it a way to use information from
earlier elements when processing later ones.

## Technical explanation

A basic RNN updates hidden state as $h_t=f(W_xx_t+W_hh_{t-1}+b)$ and
produces outputs from the current state. Training commonly uses
backpropagation through time. Simple RNNs can struggle with long-range
dependencies because gradients may vanish or explode.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

RNNs established important approaches to sequential modeling and remain
useful in some streaming or compact sequence applications. LSTMs, GRUs, and
Transformers address limitations of the basic recurrent architecture in
different ways.

## How it works

The same recurrent transformation is applied at each time step. The hidden
state summarizes information from the preceding sequence prefix, and the
model can emit an output at every step or only at selected positions.
Padding, masking, and sequence length need careful handling in batches.

## Practical example

A basic RNN can read sensor readings in order and update a hidden state
after each observation. For long sequences, engineers often compare gated
RNNs or attention-based models and measure performance under realistic
sequence lengths.

## Common misconceptions

- The hidden state is a learned summary, not a perfect memory of all earlier
  inputs.
- RNNs can process variable-length sequences, but they process time steps
  sequentially and may be harder to parallelize than Transformers.
